This page explains what this site collects about your visit, and what it deliberately doesn't. If anything below is unclear, email me at [hello@leedurbin.co.nz](mailto:hello@leedurbin.co.nz) or [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/lddurbin/twelve_days_to_deming/issues).

## Analytics

This site uses [Simple Analytics](https://www.simpleanalytics.com/) to see, in aggregate, which pages get read. It's built to collect as little as possible:

- **No cookies.** Simple Analytics doesn't set any, so no cookie banner is needed.
- **EU-hosted**, outside the advertising-data ecosystem that most mainstream analytics tools sit inside.
- **No personal data.** It records that a page was viewed, not who viewed it — there's no identifier that ties one of your visits to the next.
- **Honours Do Not Track.** If your browser sends a Do Not Track signal, Simple Analytics drops your visit entirely rather than collecting a reduced version of it. That's a deliberate choice on this site's part, not the vendor's default behaviour on its own — it means the numbers I see slightly undercount real readers, which I'd rather have than override anyone's stated preference.

A small number of named actions on this site — for example, opening the feedback email link or turning on the dyslexia-friendly font — are also sent to Simple Analytics as events, so I can tell whether specific features are actually being used. These events carry no more identifying information than a page view does.

## What stays on your device

Your reading preferences — light/dark theme and the dyslexia-friendly font toggle — are saved with your browser's `localStorage`, not sent to me or anyone else. The same is true of your progress through the Day 3 funnel experiment, if you've used it. This data lives only in your browser and is used only to restore your preferences and progress the next time you open the site.

Clearing your browser's site data for this page (or using it in a private/incognito window) resets all of it.

## Why any of this exists at all

This course spends a full day on the danger of managing by numbers you don't understand, so I'm cautious about instrumenting the site that teaches it. The intent here is narrow: find out where readers get stuck or drop off, and check whether the accessibility features are actually being used — not to build a dashboard for its own sake.
